task:
BUILD PURGE PR P2d: the disposable 1% purge rehearsal that measures the figures the production plan needs, run on the Contabo self-hosted runners (owner decision 2026-10-16). Base on current origin/main; it must be ebe88b78ec66f9eeacc1576a5d3b535a312be166 (PR #822, P2c, merged) -- record the SHA you used. New branch (no target_branch). You build the workflow and harness; you do NOT dispatch it. No production access, no production credentials, no V3_PRODUCTION_* or ED_NEW_OPERATOR_* secrets anywhere in this workflow.

AUTHORITY: docs/development/v3-governed-derived-purge-design.md -- section 4.4 items 4 and 7 (crash/interruption rehearsal and integration-scale rehearsal), section 7 gates 4 (about 1% of production scale, peaks x1.5) and 10 (rewrites authorized only after the crash rehearsal shows a crash mid-rewrite leaves the old or the new relation intact, never half-swapped), section 4.2 (what the plan must carry: per-relation rows_per_second, rewrite_allowance_seconds, rewrite peak bytes, per-batch peak filesystem growth (WAL+temp, must be < 1 GB or the batch bound is lowered), autovacuum budget bytes, per-relation rewrite statement timeout). Read CLAUDE.md first (Contabo hosts exactly three self-hosted Codex runners and is not production). Read the merged action: scripts/operator/actions/v3-derived-generation-purge.sh and scripts/operator/lib/v3_generation_purge.py, v3_purge_transactions.py, v3_purge_delete.py, v3_purge_rewrite*.py; and how the plan consumes delete[relation].* and rewrite figures.

BUILD:
1. .github/workflows/v3-derived-purge-rehearsal.yml: workflow_dispatch only; runs-on the existing self-hosted Contabo runner labels used by .github/workflows/codex-laptop.yml ([self-hosted, Linux, X64]); permissions contents: read; concurrency group v3-derived-purge-rehearsal (cancel-in-progress false); timeout bounded and documented; checkout exact main. Inputs: scale (choice: smoke = ~0.05% for a quick check, one_percent = the real rehearsal; default smoke). First step refuses unless free disk on the Docker data root is >= 40 GB for one_percent (>= 5 GB for smoke), Docker is reachable without sudo, and no other rehearsal container exists; always cleans up its own containers/volumes in an if: always() step and verifies they are gone. No secrets.
2. A rehearsal harness (e.g. scripts/rehearsal/v3_derived_purge_rehearsal.py, CPython 3.14) that: starts a disposable PostgreSQL 18 container with a unique name and a dedicated volume (pinned image digest consistent with the repo's other PG18 usage) and configuration close to production's relevant settings (wal_level, archive off is acceptable but record it; autovacuum on); applies the committed V3 migration lineage through 016 from sql/v3/migration-manifest.txt; seeds synthetic data shaped like production for the four payload relations (system_search, economy_opportunity, body_mechanics, system_rating_vector) with two target generations (BUILDING/VALIDATING) and one published generation whose survivor rows must remain untouched, at the requested scale (one_percent ~ 2,000,000 systems; derive per-relation row counts from the committed 2026-10-10 lifecycle receipt proportions under docs/operations/evidence/ and record them), plus the cluster/archetype tables empty of targets. Then it drives the REAL action (not a re-implementation) against this disposable database in an explicit rehearsal/target-override mode that is impossible to point at production: the override must require a disposable-marker the action checks (for example a database comment or a v3_meta row the harness creates and production never has, plus a hostname/container check), must be refused by default, and must be covered by tests proving production identities never accept it. Sequence: plan -> authorize -> verify-system-archetype-empty -> per relation: delete (to completion, measuring) -> rewrite -> complete.
3. Measurements recorded per relation: rows_per_second for deletes; per-batch peak filesystem growth on the data volume (WAL + temp; sample free bytes at a short interval during each batch); peak growth during VACUUM (FULL, ANALYZE) and its duration; autovacuum budget (measure autovacuum after an equivalent delete on a throwaway copy, or document and use the design's lower bound of current heap+index bytes if measuring is impractical -- say which); statement durations. Apply the design's 1.5x margin where it says so, and scale to production by the recorded proportion, keeping the raw figures too.
4. Crash/interruption rehearsals (gate 10 and 4.4 item 4): kill the batch client before and after commit; terminate VACUUM FULL mid-rewrite via the monitor and via pg_terminate_backend; restart PostgreSQL mid-rewrite (docker restart) -- each time prove exactly one old-or-new relation state (never half-swapped), unchanged published counts, and that re-dispatch resolves correctly (relfilenode comparison, recovered ANALYZE, no double rewrite); kill the wrapper between VACUUM FULL commit and REWRITE_VERIFIED and prove recovery. Record pass/fail per scenario.
5. Output: a sealed rehearsal receipt (scripts/operator/lib/f2d_evidence.py seal) containing source SHA, scale, image digest, settings, row counts, per-relation figures (raw and margin-applied), the crash-scenario results and a boolean gate_10_crash_rehearsal_passed; uploaded as an artifact with retention 180 days. Add the code path by which a reviewed rehearsal receipt (path + sha256) feeds the production plan's delete[relation].rows_per_second / rows_per_second_source / rewrite_allowance_seconds / autovacuum_budget_bytes / per-batch reservation / rewrite peak / statement timeout figures (plan mode input; plan refuses figures from a receipt whose gate_10 flag is false or whose seal fails).
6. Tests: workflow contract tests (dispatch-only, self-hosted labels, no secrets, disk refusal, cleanup always, concurrency); harness unit tests (seeding proportions, measurement math, margin application, receipt schema); the rehearsal override cannot be enabled against production identities; plan consumption of a valid/invalid rehearsal receipt. A small CI-runnable PG18 smoke of the harness at tiny scale is welcome if it fits the Finder PG18 lane budget (~34 of 45 minutes used) -- otherwise a separate small CI job.
7. Docs: runbook section 'P2d rehearsal' (how to dispatch smoke then one_percent, what to review, how the receipt feeds plan) and CHANGES.md.

RULES: CPython 3.14; fail-closed; parameterized SQL; no secrets; no production operation; do not weaken existing tests. Run: ruff check .; bash -n on changed scripts; python -m pytest -q on touched tests plus the purge test files and workflow contract tests; python scripts/operator/v3_production_deploy.py --operation authority-gate; the Semgrep command from .github/workflows/semgrep.yml. If Docker is available on your runner, run the harness at smoke scale and include its receipt summary.

IF YOU CANNOT FINISH EVERYTHING: (1) safe rehearsal override with production-refusal tests; (2) harness seeding + happy-path sequence + measurements + receipt; (3) workflow; (4) crash scenarios; (5) plan consumption; (6) docs. End with: base SHA; files changed; how the override is made impossible against production; tests run with counts; whether a smoke run was executed and its figures; anything left.
